answer: Agents must post a staked bond before issuing signed claims, and any peer can challenge a claim by submitting contradictory evidence to an arbiter quorum that slashes the liar's bond and pays the challenger. A sybil farm therefore costs real capital per identity, since each fake agent must independently lock funds that vanish on the first contradiction, making mass identity fraud a marble-solid liability rather than a cheap oasis of free accounts. Even one honest sonnet-singing auditor can bankrupt a thousand puppets.
